title: Trace gateway, channel, fan-out, and presence failures
description: Select a failure to see which path remains authoritative, which work can retry, and what the sender or recipient should actually see.

nodes.label: Sender app
nodes.detail: Creates one client message ID, sends the command over a persistent session, and retries that same identity after an uncertain response.

nodes.label: Gateway fleet
nodes.detail: Authenticates the session, applies rate limits, tracks subscriptions and cursors, and forwards channel commands without becoming message history authority.

nodes.label: Channel owner
nodes.detail: Serializes accepted writes for one channel partition, checks current membership, assigns the next channel sequence, and rejects conflicting ownership.

nodes.label: Message log and outbox
nodes.detail: Commits the message and its fan-out event together. A successful append is the sender acknowledgement boundary and the replay source.

nodes.label: Fan-out workers
nodes.detail: Consume accepted messages, resolve active gateway subscriptions, retry at least once, and expose queue age without changing channel sequence order.

nodes.label: Presence service
nodes.detail: Tracks online status, typing, and session leases with short expiration. It can become unknown without invalidating durable membership or message history.

nodes.label: Recipient gateways
nodes.detail: Push each envelope to currently attached clients, suppress duplicate message IDs, and retain a replay cursor for every subscribed channel.

nodes.label: Recipient app
nodes.detail: Displays only contiguous channel sequences, requests a missing range after reconnect, and shows explicit connecting, delayed, or presence-unknown states.

scenarios.label: Healthy delivery
scenarios.summary: The gateway forwards one idempotent command, the channel owner assigns order, the durable append succeeds, and fan-out targets active recipient sessions.
scenarios.result: The sender receives an accepted acknowledgement after durability. Recipients deduplicate retries and display the next contiguous channel sequence promptly.

scenarios.label: Gateway zone loss
scenarios.summary: Part of the gateway fleet disappears. Sessions reconnect to healthy capacity and resend uncertain commands with the original message ID and last received channel cursor.
scenarios.result: Affected clients briefly show Connecting. Duplicate sends return the original accepted result, and recipients replay from their cursor instead of losing or reordering messages.

scenarios.label: Channel owner stalls
scenarios.summary: The partition that owns one channel cannot commit the next sequence before the deadline. Routing around it would create two possible ordering authorities.
scenarios.result: The sender sees Sending or Retry, not a false success. No unsequenced event reaches fan-out; other channel partitions continue while this hot channel recovers or moves ownership safely.

scenarios.label: Fan-out backlog
scenarios.summary: Messages continue to commit, but recipient delivery workers consume more slowly than accepted events arrive. The durable log preserves the replay order.
scenarios.result: Senders may still see accepted messages while recipients see delayed synchronization. Shed typing and presence traffic, isolate hot partitions, add consumers, and replay durable messages in channel order.

scenarios.label: Presence unavailable
scenarios.summary: Session leases and typing updates are unavailable, but durable channel membership, message order, and history remain healthy dependencies.
scenarios.result: Messages continue through known subscriptions and cursor replay. Clients show presence as Unknown and disable or age out typing indicators instead of hiding channel history.

scenarios.label: Recipient gateway loss
scenarios.summary: The message is durable and fan-out reaches the recipient edge, but the attached gateway fails before the client advances its local cursor.
scenarios.result: The recipient briefly shows Connecting, resumes from the last contiguous sequence on another gateway, and suppresses any duplicate envelope delivered during replay.
